name: 28451-batchdecode-qwen35-35ba3bfp8-1gpu
model: Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8, the checkpoint's own block-wise-FP8 release. Ungated; ~35 GB of weights in 14 shards.
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, one node, one GPU.
parallelism: tp1. No tensor, pipeline, expert or data parallelism.
architecture: Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration, a GDN-hybrid MoE; the rest is in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, warmup the first 15%, bounded at 2560 requests with a 3600 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no shared prefix: 256 prompt tokens in, 512 output tokens out, both fixed, no spread, `ignore_eos: true`. Prompts are unique. Seed 42.
purpose: A 35-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts chat assistant writing long replies for 256 concurrent users on one H100.
launch:
# sglang server arguments. Flat `key: value` only -- a nested block is DROPPED by the reader.
# host/port/served-model-name are set by the serving layer, not here.

model-path: Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8

tp-size: 1

# With the prefix cache off, this is simultaneously the recurrent-state pool size and the
# admission ceiling. Left unset the pool auto-fits to whatever memory is free and the ceiling
# lands wherever that falls, which is not reproducible.
max-running-requests: 256
disable-radix-cache: true

# 256 is the top of the tp<4 / 80 GB decode capture ladder; above it decode drops to eager.
cuda-graph-max-bs-decode: 256

# The longest request is 256 + 512 = 768, so nothing is truncated. Load-bearing rather than
# cosmetic: the checkpoint advertises 262144 positions and the engine sizes device-side
# per-request tables from that number.
context-length: 4096

# Deliberately below the usual 0.85. Do not raise it.
mem-fraction-static: 0.75

random-seed: 42
